messages:
Sam K: kicking off bring-up for Mantis-multi-v0 (text+image concat embeddings). brief: eval harness showed odd downshift in cosine similarity for image-text pairs after per-tower quantization. anyone seen this pattern before?
Priya N: saw something like that when we quantized the vision tower separately and forgot to re-normalize before concatenation. can you share the eval outputs? :mag:
Sam K: pasted quick results: recall@1 text->image: 0.62 -> 0.49 after quant; recall@5 0.83 -> 0.72. silhouette score on combined clusters dropped 0.18 -> 0.05. baseline float32 numbers on the same dataset.
Miguel R: ouch. what quant config? perchannel symmetric? int6?
Sam K: per-channel int6 symmetric for vision, text kept float16. using concat(text_norm, image_norm) in codepath but it looks like normals got skipped in compiled kernel path.
Li Wang: can you paste the exact embedding pipeline snippet? might be a runtime fusing bug.
Sam K: sure:
```
# pseudo
text_e = text_encoder(tokens)          # float16
img_e = vision_encoder(image)         # int6 after quant
if config.normalize:                 # expected
    text_e = l2_normalize(text_e)
    img_e = l2_normalize(img_e)
emb = concat(text_e, img_e)
```
But in quant path img_e was returned unnormed (we think) by compiled kernel.
Zoe P: embed-ci-bot just ran a smoke with smaller sample and logged distances. embed-ci-bot: `CI: multimodal-smoke/172 samples - delta mean cosine -0.071, std 0.012, top1 drop 13%`
Priya N: that aligns with not normalizing — magnitude changes after quantization. can you run a quick patch where we explicitly call normalize in python prior to any fused op?
Sam K: started a job: `eval/run_multimodal.py --model mantis-multi-v0 --quant vision:int6 --force-normalize`
Miguel R: while that's running, two quick sanity checks: 1) compute pairwise L2 norms pre/post quant on vision embeddings; 2) check cosine vs dot product histograms. mismatch indicates missing normalization.
Li Wang: ran a few local checks: pre-quant vision L2 mean 1.01, post-quant mean 0.62. so magnitude compressed.
Zoe P: results from Sam's job: recall@1 went back up: 0.61, recall@5 0.82, silhouette 0.16. still a slight gap vs baseline but much better.
Sam K: looks like explicit normalize fixed most. leaving open: why compiled kernel returned unnormalized vecs. filing issue with eng-runtime.
Priya N: also try calibration table with asymmetric quant for vision; sometimes symmetric per-channel compresses sign distribution for that layer. run A/B with `--quant-mode=asymmetric`
Miguel R: adding a small post-quant scale-rescale trick helped earlier: multiply embeddings by scalar learned on minibatch to restore norm distribution. hacky but useful as fallback.
embed-ci-bot: test report uploaded: https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/reports/mantis-multi/1739123456. includes knn recall, silhouette, ARI, pca/umap images.
Li Wang: filed ENG-RUNTIME ticket #4221 with kernel trace + repro. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility.
Sam K: plan: 1) keep python-side normalize as safety net in patch; 2) run larger holdout A/B (10k) with both symmetric/asymmetric int6 quant; 3) get runtime team fix for kernel. any objections?
Priya N: sounds good. also add a small unit test in the embedding harness to assert mean L2 near 1.0 +/- 0.08 after quant path.
Zoe P: noted — will add CI assertion and chart to the model page. :white_check_mark:
Miguel R: nice catch. once runtime fix lands we should re-run entire eval battery (multilang, short-query, long-query).
Sam K: thanks all — keeping thread open until ENG-RUNTIME closes ticket or A/B finishes.
